findings.title: Price falls into the thickest new 76K pile; thin supply down to 66K
findings.lean_why: Half of the thickest layer, bought only in October, is already underwater and is taking small losses; if it fails, there is no thick pile to absorb selling between here and 66K.
findings.what: Question: price has fallen into the thickest short-term holder bucket — will this layer defend or capitulate? The close of 76,676 sits inside 76–78K, where CheckOnChain (actual coin age, data date Nov 2) shows 594K short-term BTC, the largest of the 3.688M held by short-term holders. Their average cost is 75,229 (CheckOnChain); bitcoin-data publishes 75,809 (Oct 27). The close is only 1.9% / 1.1% above them.
findings.why: Two points in time (modeled, Oct 2 → Nov 1): of the 3.673M BTC held by short-term holders then, 1.060M have moved; the 1.309M bought since and not yet moved sit at 80K (472K), 76K (279K) and 82K (202K). So most of the 76K layer was bought in late October, with a cost right at the current price. Behavior: STH-SOPR 0.9978 (Nov 2), below 1 for 4 days; short-term holder realized loss 3,477 BTC vs profit 4,044 BTC (ratio 1.16, 2.8 a week ago; losses +75.5% over 7 days); network-wide daily realized profit/loss averaged 0.941 over the last 7 days (see 2026-11-02-2). Cost map: the modeled long-liquidation band is 75,200–76,300 (1.4% below the close; modeled, OKX only); the order book shows $258M of bids at 76,000 and $121M at 75,000 (Hyperliquid perp, 00:06 UTC); the Nov 13 74K put (3,850 BTC) is the largest single downside options strike.
findings.alt: Paper losses do not mean selling: the 76K newcomers may hold, and a SOPR of 0.9978 is mild loss-taking, not capitulation. The change breakdown is modeled: modeled STH total differs from actual by 0.0%, 6.9% sits in the wrong bucket, and modeled cost differs from bitcoin-data by −0.1%. URPD data date Nov 1; per-UTXO, so wallet moves after Binance reopened withdrawals on Nov 1 may count as turnover. bitcoin-data's STH cost is from Oct 27, about 6 days behind.
findings.history: This long/short holder split only exists on the site since 2026-10-27, so there are no comparable past samples; the price-near-thickest-pile and price-near-STH-cost signals appeared for the first time today.
findings.so: Scenarios (conditional, CheckOnChain Nov 2): at a 76,000 close, about 2.478M short-term BTC (about 67%) would be underwater; down to 66,000 that only rises to 2.600M (+122K, thin supply); at 64,000 it jumps to 3.012M (+412K). Logic chain: October's turnover stacked new supply at 76–82K, so this range has holders on both sides; this layer is taking small losses while dollars are not returning, so support is not yet confirmed; if 76K and the STH cost give way, supply is thin down to 66K and the modeled long-liquidation band sits right at 75–76K — liquidations are market sells and could speed a drop. The market stage and exit framework have not moved.
findings.next: By Nov 9: a close below 75,000 means the 76K layer and STH cost have failed — confirms; a close back above 78,000 puts price above the thickest pile — refutes.

findings.title: Sellers as a whole are now taking losses; profit-taking has ebbed
findings.lean_why: Sellers have flipped from taking profits to realizing losses, meaning top buyers are starting to give up; this usually shows up in weak consolidation and does not mean the cycle has turned bearish.
findings.what: CheckOnChain network-wide daily realized profit ÷ realized loss: Oct 29 0.836, Oct 30 0.622, Oct 31 1.128, Nov 1 0.656, Nov 2 0.762; the last-7-day average is 0.941, below 1. On Oct 21 it was 3.247. The 90-day average of 2.349 is still above 1 (since Sep 4, 59 days); if the daily ratio stays at 0.941, the 90-day average would drop below 1 around 2027-01-19 (a projection).
findings.why: The pipeline did not flag this as a signal; the basis is onchain.rpl in the brief. Cross-check: CoinMetrics net realized P/L was −$314M on Nov 1 (1-year percentile 27.1), −$1.135B over 7 days vs +$3.779B the prior 7 days — same direction; Glassnode's BTC Market Pulse Week 45 (Nov 2, entity-adjusted) also shows the realized profit/loss ratio turning negative, with losses slightly exceeding profits. Breakdown: on the short-term holder side (CheckOnChain, smoothed) realized loss is 3,477 BTC vs profit 4,044 BTC, ratio 1.16, still slightly above 1 — so the network-wide weakening is mostly profits shrinking (−27.0% over 7 days), with losses up 75.5% second; this is not panic loss-taking.
findings.alt: Daily ratios can be inflated or depressed by exchange wallet consolidation and large transfers, and the days around Binance reopening withdrawals on Nov 1 are exactly that; the one-day bounce to 1.128 on Oct 31 shows the signal is not yet stable. The 90-day average is slow and still 2.349; the projected date assumes an unchanged daily ratio and is not a forecast.
findings.history: This cycle the 90-day average was last below 1 from 2026-02-07 to 2026-09-03 (209 days, low 0.596). A relapse after recovering: 2019-12-11 to 2020-01-16 (fell back for 37 days, 7 months after recovering above 1). Short red spells also occurred in 2014-05 (7 days) and 2022-02/03 (25 days), followed one year later by −52.1% and −32.8%; few samples, background only.
findings.so: What changed is the nature of the selling: October was profit-taking, now it is small loss-taking. What did not: the 90-day average is still above 1, and the market stage and exit framework have not moved; the 30-day cumulative net realized P/L is +$6.55B (4-year percentile 42.5), far from the cycle-level capitulation line.
findings.next: By Nov 9: a 7-day average daily ratio back above 1.2 means the loss-taking was a one-week episode — refutes; short-term holder realized loss rising above 5,000 BTC means losses are widening — confirms.

findings.title: Illiquid supply jump is mostly Binance withdrawals, not new buying
findings.lean_why: Coins leaving exchanges reduces sellable supply, but this is a defensive move; dollars are leaving at the same time and real new demand has not shown up.
findings.what: bitcoin-data illiquid supply rose from 12.679M to 12.876M BTC over 7 days (+1.55%, Nov 1; the 7-day change is at the 100th 1-year percentile); CoinMetrics exchange supply fell 1.32% over 7 days (Nov 1). Over the same period the Coinbase premium 7-day average is −0.188% (Nov 2, lowest since the series began in 2026-01, n=299), and stablecoin supply is $297.6B, −1.53% over 7 days and −$9.3B over 30 days.
findings.why: Breakdown: the drop in exchange supply is concentrated after Binance reopened withdrawals on Nov 1 (The Block: $3.64B net outflow in the first 9.5 hours; the 24-hour net outflow eased to about $3.29B on Nov 2). Coins withdrawn into fresh, unspent addresses get classified as illiquid. Cross-check: if this were new buying, US spot would be paying a premium and stablecoins would be growing — both are at their weakest; the latest complete ETF day, Oct 30, was −$643.2M. So the same coins are changing location, not demand rising.
findings.alt: Some of it could be genuine long-term buyers withdrawing on the dip; illiquidity is classified from an address's past spending, new addresses take time to settle, and the number may give back. Different providers (bitcoin-data, CoinMetrics) are not subtracted from each other; only directions are compared.
findings.history: Sharp 7-day jumps in illiquid supply happened 3 times before (2025-10-13, 2026-04-05, 2026-05-23), with 30-day moves of −11.8%, +17.4%, −16.6% afterward, median −11.8% (baseline +2.0%); sharp 7-day stablecoin drops 4 times before, 30-day median −5.4% (baseline +0.2%); too few samples, background only.
findings.so: The withdrawal wave reduces sellable coins on exchanges, removing one short-term source of supply; but it does not change the flows picture: dollars are not returning, and the buyers needed to absorb break-even selling at 80–82K have not appeared. The 'exchange supply 90-day change negative' evidence light is steadier (−0.94%), but this time it should be discounted.
findings.next: By Nov 9: a Coinbase premium 7-day average below −0.2% means US spot keeps selling — confirms; stablecoin 7-day change back to positive means dollars are returning — refutes.
